configuration: default connection, no concurrent writers, new local disposable database
command_argv:
import json, sqlite3, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from src import adapter
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
 p=str(Path(tmp)/"probe.sqlite")
 adapter.apply(p,[{"sku":"old","quantity":2}])
 success=adapter.apply(p,[{"sku":"a","quantity":3},{"sku":"b","quantity":4}])
 with sqlite3.connect(p) as db: before=db.execute("SELECT * FROM inventory ORDER BY sku").fetchall()
 try: adapter.apply(p,[{"sku":"c","quantity":5},{"sku":"bad","quantity":-1}])
 except ValueError as e: error=str(e)
 with sqlite3.connect(p) as db: after=db.execute("SELECT * FROM inventory ORDER BY sku").fetchall()
 print(json.dumps({"success":success,"before":before,"failure":error,"after":after,"partial_write_visible":before!=after}))
conclusion: This adapter commits each applied row; a later invalid record leaves prior writes visible to a fresh connection. Applying directly to the visible destination cannot satisfy all-or-nothing failure. This says nothing about an unimplemented staging/publication/recovery design.
